title: Own a pharmacy business only as a pharmacist, under a pharmacy business licence
what: Only a pharmacist (or another person the Act allows) may own, or hold an interest in, a pharmacy business. In Queensland the owner must also hold a pharmacy business licence for the business.

sources.title: Pharmacy Business Ownership Act 2024 (Qld)
sources.quote: 16 Who may hold material interest in pharmacy business A person must not hold a material interest in a pharmacy business unless— (a) the person is a practising pharmacist; or (b) the person is a close adult relative of a practising pharmacist and the practising pharmacist holds an interest in the business. Maximum penalty—200 penalty units.

sources.title: Pharmacy Business Ownership Act 2024 (Qld)
sources.quote: 15 Owner of pharmacy business must hold pharmacy business licence (1) A person must not own a pharmacy business unless the person holds a pharmacy business licence for the business that is in effect. Maximum penalty—200 penalty units.

sources.title: Pharmacy Business Ownership Act 2024 (Qld)
sources.quote: 16 Who may hold material interest in pharmacy business A person must not hold a material interest in a pharmacy business unless— (a) the person is a practising pharmacist; or (b) the person is a close adult relative of a practising pharmacist and the practising pharmacist holds an interest in the business. Maximum penalty—200 penalty units.

confidence_note: The Act's own words reserve material interests in pharmacy businesses to pharmacists and their close relatives.

assessment.summary: A new licensing regime and council enforce Queensland's rules on who may own a pharmacy. It adds a licensing layer and tightens enforcement of ownership limits that keep out other business models.

marks.reason: A new pharmacy business licence and enforced ownership limits restrict who may open or buy a pharmacy.
Owners must hold a licence and report material interests.
